ety.text: From Middle English schrynken, from Old English sċrincan, from Proto-Germanic *skrinkwaną. Cognate with Dutch schrinken (“to shrink”). The sense “psychologist, psychotherapist” is a clipping of head-shrinker.

ex: The bottom line is this: To shrink your gut, you need to start listening to it.
This garment will shrink when wet.
I have not found that water, by mixture of ashes, will shrink or draw into less room.
Molly shrank away from the blows of the whip.
The Libyc Hammon ſhrinks his horn,

senses.d: To withdraw or retire, as from danger.
ex: What happier natures shrink at with affright, / The hard inhabitant contends is right.
They assisted us against the Thebans when you shrank from the task.

senses.d: To move back or away, especially because of fear or disgust.

ex: Yet almost with, with sudden shrink, That I had less to praise.
You need to see a shrink, you crazy fool.
My shrink said that he was an enabler, bad for me.

senses.d: Loss of inventory, for example due to shoplifting or not selling items before their expiration date.
